Banner of Truth
BAN-er uv trooth
proper noun (a Reformed publisher)
From Psalm 60:4, “a banner… because of the truth”; the Banner of Truth Trust, a Reformed publishing ministry founded in 1957 to republish the Puritans and Reformed classics.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Banner of Truth Trust is a Reformed publishing ministry, founded in Britain in 1957, devoted to republishing the works of the Puritans, the Reformers, and the great Reformed and experimental divines, together with sound contemporary literature, for the recovery of doctrinal and experimental Christianity. Its name is taken from the Psalm: “Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, that it may be displayed because of the truth.” The dictionary honours the Banner of Truth as a chief instrument, under God, of the twentieth-century recovery of Reformed and Puritan literature, putting back into the hands of pastors and people the writings of Owen, Bunyan, the Westminster divines, the Scottish and English Puritans, and the Reformers—treasures long out of print. By such republishing it has served the church's sanctification through the truth, for the Lord prayed, “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth,” and the apostle charged that the sound words be committed to faithful men able to teach others. The dictionary commends the ministry of preserving and spreading sound doctrine in print as a faithful application of the command to buy the truth and sell it not. As with any publisher, its books are to be read with discernment, weighed by Scripture, and not received uncritically merely for the imprint; but the Banner's great and abiding service has been to display the banner of truth in an age of doctrinal famine—keeping before the church the rich, God-centred, experimental divinity of the Reformation and Puritan heritage, that a new generation might recover the old paths.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The Reformed publishing trust (founded 1957) devoted to republishing the Puritans and Reformed classics; named from Psalm 60:4, a chief instrument of the modern recovery of Reformed and experimental literature, read with discernment under Scripture.

📖 Key Scripture

Ps 60:4 — "Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, that it may be displayed because of the truth. Selah."

Joh 17:17 — "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth."

2 Ti 2:2 — "And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the only caution is that books are weighed by Scripture, not received uncritically for the imprint.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle the Banner of Truth serves is the sanctification of the church through the truth, and the preservation and spread of sound doctrine in print. The dictionary honours the trust as a chief instrument, under God, of the twentieth-century recovery of Reformed and Puritan literature—restoring to pastors and people the writings of Owen, Bunyan, the Westminster divines, and the Reformers, long out of print. The Lord prayed that His people be sanctified through the truth, and the apostle charged that sound words be committed to faithful men; the ministry of faithful republishing applies the command to buy the truth and sell it not.

The only caution the dictionary marks is the one proper to every publisher: books are to be read with discernment and weighed by Scripture, not received uncritically merely for the imprint, however worthy the press. No publisher is infallible, and even a sound catalogue contains works of varying weight. That said, the Banner's great and abiding service has been to display the banner of truth in an age of doctrinal famine—keeping before the church the rich, God-centred, experimental divinity of the Reformation and Puritan heritage, that a new generation might recover the old paths and walk in them.
